svg.title: HashMap with broken equals / hashCode
svg.desc: Three failure scenarios, each with a 16-bucket table. 1, equals() without hashCode(): map.put(new Emp(1, "Asha"), "dev") hashes from the identity hash code to bucket 3; map.get(new Emp(1, "Asha")) gets a different identity hash, bucket 11, which is empty, so it returns null. Equal objects end up in different buckets: get() returns null and a HashSet keeps duplicates. 2, a mutable key changed after put(): put(key) with id = 1 goes to bucket 3; then key.setId(2) makes its hash point to bucket 7; get(key) searches bucket 7 and returns null; the entry is stuck in bucket 3, an unreachable entry and a memory leak. 3, hashCode() returns a constant: every entry lands in bucket 0, a long chain or tree; still correct but slow, O(n), or O(log n) once treeified with Comparable keys, instead of O(1). Footer rules: equal objects must have equal hash codes; use immutable keys, records are ideal.
